raw_response:
I farm the same wheat-maize rotation every year, so I do not start from zero. I start from what has worked on land like mine in Quzhou, then I adjust a little for cost, water, and how much grain I want to hold onto. I have 30 mu and a well, so I will not farm too light. If I save too much on fertilizer and water, the loss in yield is bigger than the money I saved. For wheat, I will hold the stand steady, use an improved variety, put enough bottom fertilizer in, then chase the crop again at jointing with water. Wheat here can give good yield if I do not let it dry out at the key stages. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people around here, grab the season quickly after wheat harvest, keep the field clean, and feed it enough nitrogen for ear growth. I will not push to demonstration-field levels, because that costs money and management, but I will aim above an ordinary careless field. All the fertilizer numbers below are pure nutrient per mu.

For wheat I will use improved seed, enough base fertilizer, three irrigations around key stages, and three pesticide passes because protecting the stand is cheaper than losing yield. For maize I will use hybrid seed, rush sowing after wheat harvest with no-tillage, keep nitrogen steady for ear growth, give two irrigations if rain is not enough, and spray twice for the main pests and diseases. I will aim for solid farm yield, not extreme demonstration yield, because I still have to watch the full household budget."
